lyrics:
[Intro: four drum hits, boom, ba-boom, crack, then wall of sound]

[Verse 1: young lead, trembling vibrato, castanets]
First time I saw you by the record machine
You had a nickel and I had a dream
You played the one I would have played
I knew right then the plans I'd made

[Pre-Chorus: backing voices rise, strings swell]
So if you want to find me
You know the place

[Chorus: lead and backing voices, the full wall]
Meet me, meet me at the jukebox
(Meet me at the jukebox)
Pick the one we know
(Whoa, oh, oh, oh)
Meet me at the jukebox
And don't let go

[Verse 2: same voice, the same tune, decades later]
Fifty years and the diner's gone
Somebody else's name is on
The sign, but I still know the spot
Where you said "yes" and I said "what?"

[Pre-Chorus: backing voices rise, strings swell]
So if you want to find me
You know the place

[Chorus: lead and backing voices, the full wall]
Meet me, meet me at the jukebox
(Meet me at the jukebox)
Pick the one we know
(Whoa, oh, oh, oh)
Meet me at the jukebox
And don't let go

[Instrumental: strings play the chorus melody, castanets]

[Break: everything stops, the four drum hits again]

[Final Chorus: everyone, lead ad-libbing over the top]
Meet me, meet me at the jukebox
(Meet me at the jukebox)
Pick the one we know
(Whoa, oh, oh, oh)
Meet me at the jukebox
And don't let go

[Outro: backing hook repeating, long echo, fade]
(Whoa, oh, oh, oh)
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 130 BPM, 4/4, E major. A grand, swaying beat with a Latin lilt. Enormous and innocent at once.

VOICE: A young woman with a bright, nasal, slightly tough New York voice and a fast, trembling vibrato on held notes. Three more women sing the echoes and the wordless 'whoa' hook behind her, soaked in echo. She ad-libs over the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A drum kit that opens the record alone with four hits: kick, two kicks, and a snare with a handclap. Then a 'wall of sound': several pianos, several guitars, two basses, horns and a full string section all playing together in a large echo chamber. Castanets, maracas and tambourine throughout.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the four drum hits twice, then everything. 0:08 Verse 1. 0:30 Pre-chorus. 0:38 Chorus 1. 1:00 Verse 2. 1:22 Pre-chorus. 1:30 Chorus 2. 1:52 Instrumental, strings on the tune. 2:06 Break: everything stops for the four drum hits. 2:10 Final chorus with ad-libs. 2:30 Outro, the backing hook in a long echo, fading by 2:40.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1960s Los Angeles wall of sound: mono, dense and drenched in echo, with instruments blended into one roar and the voice riding on top.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The four drum hits at the very start, and again at 2:06.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The second verse is sung fifty years on in the same girlish melody. That is the experience of hearing the original now: the voice stays seventeen and the listener does not.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Hope, a leap of half a century, constancy.
